body.text: The Wallabies have been humiliated by the All Blacks via a 50-19 thumping in the opening Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park.
The victory means the All Blacks retain the Bledisloe Cup for yet another year, having held the precious silverware since 2003.
They also pushed their winning streak over the Wallabies out to 12 Tests and gave coach Dave Rennie a triumph in his first meeting with his former side.
Despite arriving in Auckland in a buoyant mood, the Les Kiss-coached Wallabies will return to Australia with their tail between their legs.
Their hopes of ending a 40-year losing streak against the All Blacks at Eden Park were dashed after the home side ran rampant in the second half.
Holding a slender 17-14 lead at the break, the All Blacks scored five tries to one in the second term to record a deserved victory at their spiritual home.
The All Blacks scored seven tries in total, with Damian McKenzie adding six conversions and a penalty goal.
The Wallabies began strongly, scoring a brilliant try from Tom Wright in the seventh minute of play.
Ryan Lonergan added the extras to make the score 7-0, but the All Blacks replied with converted tries from back-rowers Peter Lakai and Tupou Vaa'i.

McKenzie's 32nd-minute penalty goal extended the All Blacks' lead to 17-7, but Wallabies captain Harry Wilson scored under the posts in the shadows of half-time to keep his side in touch on the scoreboard.
Once All Blacks scrum half Cam Roigard scored eight minutes after half-time, however, the floodgates opened.
Tries from captain Codie Taylor, Leroy Carter and Josh Moorby followed, before the Wallabies managed a consolation five-pointer from reserve hooker Josh Nasser.
Will Jordan touched down for the final All Blacks' try only moments before full-time, icing the convincing win.
The Wallabies' six-match unbeaten run came to an abrupt end, with the defeat serving as a bitter reality check.
Adding to the Wallabies' woes was the loss of star centre Len Ikitau, who failed an HIA in the first half.
The result gave Kiss his first defeat since taking over as Wallabies coach from Joe Schmidt.
Kiss and his players will have to re-group quickly as both sides meet again next Saturday at Sydney's Stadium Australia.
